title.narrative: Joint Labour Migration Program PHASE II
Joint Labour Migration Program Phase II

description.narrative: Joint Labor Migration Programme utformades och lanserades 2018 med det övergripande målet att förbättra styrningen av arbetskraftsmigration för att uppnå en säker och ordnad migration i Afrika i enlighet med relevanta ramar för Afrikanska Unionen (AU) och regionala ekonomiska kommissioner (RECs), såväl som i enlighet med internationella överenskommelser. Den andra fasen av Joint Labour Migration Program (JLMP II), bygger på det betydande arbete som gjorts under den första fasen av programmet och på det politiska stöd som gavs programmet av afrikanerna statschefer och regeringar under AUs 24:e ordinarie sessionen i januari 2015. Joint Labour Migration Programme bidrar till att stärka den afrikanska policys kring arbetsmigration och den institutionella miljön genom att strategiskt förbättra kapaciteten hos Afrikanska Unionens Kommission (AUC) och RECs och deras samordning med medlemsstaterna och likasinnade intressenter, och genom att stödja samrådet på regional och nationell nivå. Genom JLMP-projektet har kapacitet och färdigheter stärkts genom dialog, medvetandegörande och kapacitetsutvecklingsinsatser, särskilt workshops för arbetsgivar- och arbetstagarorganisationer och statistikansvariga som hölls 2019. Inrättandet av den rådgivande arbetsmigrationskommittén (LMAC), samordningen med Global Forum for Migration Development (GFMD) och Abu Dhabi Dialogue, och ambassadörernas möten bidrar till framväxten av en gemensam vision om hur man kan bistå migrerande arbetare. Resultaten som det svenska stödet förväntas bidra till är: Outcome 1: Stärkt, effektiv, rättighetsbaserad och genderkänslig styrning och reglering av arbetskraftsmigration för migrerande arbetstagare oavsett gender i Afrika. Outcome 2: Migrerande arbetstagare oavsett gender i både formella och informella sektorer åtnjuter humana och säkra arbetsmiljöer, tillgång till och överföring av socialt skydd och sociala förmåner och ömsesidigt erkännande av färdigheter och kvalifikationer. Outcome 3: Förbättrad tillgänglighet och ökat utnyttjande av disaggregerad data och statistik från arbetskraftsmigration av medlemsstater och RECs för evidensbaserat beslutsfattande, policyutformande och tillämpning. Outcome 4: Stärkt styrning av JLMP. Projektets aktivitetsperiod är från april 2022 till mars 2025 med en total budget på 79 000 000 SEK.

The Joint Labour Migration Program was developed and launched in 2018 with the overall objective of improving the governance of labour migration to achieve safer, orderly and regular migration in Africa as committed in relevant frameworks of the African Union (AU) and Regional Economic Commissions (RECs), as well as international labour conventions and other cooperation processes. The second phase of Joint Labour Migration Program (JLMP II) relies on the significant work done in the first phase of the Program and on the political support that was adopted by the Africans Heads of State and the Governments during the 24th Ordinary Session of the African Union (AU) Assembly in January 2015.The Joint Labour Migration Program contributes to strengthening the African labour migration governance policy and institutional environment by strategically improving the capacities of the AUC and the RECs and their coordination with member states and like-minded stakeholders, and by supporting consultation and dialogue at the regional and national levels. Through the JLMP capacities and skills have been strengthened through consultations, awareness raising and capacity development events, notably the workshops of Employers’ and the Workers’ organizations and Statistical officers held in 2019. The establishing of the Labour Migration Advisory Committee (LMAC), the coordination with the Global Forum for Migration Development (GFMD) and with Abu Dhabi Dialogue, and the Ambassadors’ meetings are contributing to the emergence of a joint vision on how to assist migrant workers. The results that the Swedish support is expected to contribute to are: Outcome 1: Strengthened effective, rights based, and gender responsive governance and regulation of labour migration and mobility for migrant workers of all gender identities in Africa. Outcome 2: Migrant workers of all gender identities in both formal and informal sectors enjoy safe, humane, and secure working environments, access to and portability of social protection and social benefits, and mutual recognition of skills and qualifications. Outcome 3: Improved availability and increased utilization of labour migration disaggregated data and statistics by MS and RECs for evidence-based decision-making, policy planning, formulation, and application. Outcome 4: Strengthened governance and accountability of the JLMP. The project duration is from April 2022 to March 2025 with a total budget of 79,000,000 SEK.

The overall objective of the JLMP II Project is to contribute to the JLMP Strategic Framework (2020-2030) vision of strengthening the effective governance, and regulation of labour migration and mobility, under the rule of law, international migration law principles, and international labour standards, towards increased equitable, full-employment economic growth and sustainable development of the African Continent.
This project is deployed in close coordination with stakeholders across governments, legislatures, social partners, migrants, international organizations, the private sector, NGOs, diaspora and civil society organizations towards increased equitable economic growth and sustainable development of the African Continent.
The implementation of the project envisions four results:
Outcome 1: Strengthened effective, rights based, and gender responsive governance and regulation of labour migration and mobility for migrant workers of all gender identities in Africa.
Outcome 2: Migrant workers of all gender identities in both formal and informal sectors enjoy safe, humane, and secure working environments, access to and portability of social protection and social benefits, and mutual recognition of skills and qualifications.
Outcome 3: Improved availability and increased utilization of labour migration disaggregated data and statistics by MS and RECs for evidence-based decision-making, policy planning, formulation, and application.
Outcome 4: Strengthened governance and accountability of the JLMP.

sector.narrative: Facilitation of orderly, safe, regular and responsible migration and mobility

description.narrative:
The Sida JLMP support project, is referred to as JLMP Lead (i.e. Labour, Employment and Mobility Actions of the AU-ILO-IOM Joint Programme on Labour Migration Governance for Development and Integration in Africa). The a project is implemented in coordination with stakeholders across governments, legislators, social partners, migrants, international organizations, the private sector, non-governmental organizations, the diaspora, and civil society organizations towards increased equitable economic growth and sustainable development of the African continent. It is also closely coordinated with JLMP Action, a support project financed by the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC).
The following summary of results is a slightly edited version of the 2023 annual progress reporting from IOM to Sida submitted May 2024. According to this reporting, JLMP Lead remained flexible to accommodate the dynamics in the priorities and needs, as well as arising demands of its beneficiaries, while recommendations and lessons learnt from preceding and ongoing JLMP projects guiding decision-making. JLMP implementing partners have prioritized operationalization of recommendations from continental and regional events and consultations. Recruitment of technical staff at Regional Economic Communities (RECs) level strengthened the RECs capability to deliver.
Notable strides have been made towards the achievements of targets set in the projects results matrix and the JLMP Strategic Framework and Monitoring and Evaluation Plan (2020-2030). Accordingly, under Outcome I, support extended to the ratification of international conventions, and to the development of labour migration policy and legal frameworks by Member States (MSs) and RECs, which was complemented by assistance to establish and strengthen institutional structures and capacity building so as to reinforce implementation capacity. Further, multi-stakeholder cooperations and consultations were held to promote the protection of the human rights of migrant workers; a study was undertaken to restructure and revisit the mandate of a continental advisory arrangement; and technical assistance delivered to a regional consultative process on migration.
Under outcome II, in an effort to improve the portability of social protection services and migrant workers access to social protection mechanisms, JLMP Lead supported the development of a regulation on social security right and benefit, a study that informed the crafting of related directive and its dissemination among MSs, as well as capacity building on the same. Similarly, in order to guide MSs in the establishment of Migrant Welfare Program (MWP), capacity building modules, a compendium of best practices, a facilitator's guide, and supporting PowerPoint materials developed; capacity building support on the same delivered, and a feasibility study to establish MWP in Uganda is in progress. On the other hand, with the aim of contributing to the harmonization and recognition of occupational qualifications, trainings and experiences, the project backstopped the development of a regulation on mutual recognition of academic and professional qualifications.
Further, consultation was held to strengthen skill-based mobility for improved regular mobility pathways; geographically tailored and gender-responsive regional guides were developed for labour migration orientation programmes, a global report on migrant workers rights to freedom of association and collective bargaining was translated into French, and the first ever Africa Labour Migration Conference (ALMC) was organized.
Under Outcome III, the project strengthened the capacity of MSs, RECs and other regional and continental bodies in the collection, analysis, and dissemination of trafficking in persons and labour migration disaggregated data. It also supported the drafting of the fourth edition of the Africa Labour Migration Statistics Report and an in-depth assessment for the establishment of Labour Market Information System (LMIS) in MS.
Under Outcome IV, a steering committee meeting was held to provide strategic direction and overall guidance on the program, while a technical committee meeting reviewed JLMP Lead & Action implementation progress. A learning event that focused on taking stock of implementation of JLMP projects was organized, which informed the subsequent strategic planning meeting. With the onboarding of technical staff, especially at RECs level, the implementation capacity is further strengthening. In facilitating the integration of gender actions in labour migration policy and legal frameworks, training modules on gender-responsive labour migration policies were developed. An independent mid-term evaluation of the joint JLMP Lead and Action projects is also in progress. The evaluation preliminary findings confirms that significant progress has been made but also that there is a challenge to verify what the impact is, or will be, for the migrants themselves. The evaluation is expected to be published later in 2024. Even though implementation pace have picked up, implementation has been slower than expected during the first half of the project.
